# Configuration reference

Every setting QuickBuilder reads, generated from the product itself. Set any of them in
`appsettings.json` or as an environment variable, where `:` becomes `__`; see
[Configure](../configure.md) for how, and how to keep secrets out of files. A value that is
not allowed stops startup with a message that names the setting.

## Required

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings:Default` | `ConnectionStrings__Default` | text | *(none)* | an Npgsql connection string, e.g. `Host=db;Port=5432;Database=quickbuilder;Username=quickbuilder;Password=<password>` | <a id="connectionstrings-default"></a>**Required.** The PostgreSQL connection string. There is no default on purpose: PostgreSQL is the one external dependency and there is no sensible fallback. **Secret.** Provide it through an environment variable or a secret store, never in a file committed to version control. |

## Database

To apply migrations yourself (with `Database:AutoMigrate` set to `false`), run the `migrate`
command once per upgrade, before starting the application:

```bash
docker compose run --rm app dotnet QuickBuilder.Host.dll migrate
```

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Database:AutoMigrate` | `Database__AutoMigrate` | true/false | `true` | — | <a id="database-automigrate"></a>Apply database migrations during startup. Set `false` to apply them yourself with the `migrate` command; readiness then reports `MigrationsPending` until you do, so a half-deployed installation is visible. |
| `Database:ConnectionRetryTimeout` | `Database__ConnectionRetryTimeout` | duration (`[d.]hh:mm:ss`) | `00:02:00` | `00:00:00` – `00:30:00` | <a id="database-connectionretrytimeout"></a>How long to keep retrying an unreachable database at startup. Readiness reports `WaitingForDatabase` meanwhile. |
| `Database:ConnectionRetryDelay` | `Database__ConnectionRetryDelay` | duration (`[d.]hh:mm:ss`) | `00:00:02` | `00:00:00.100` – `00:01:00` | <a id="database-connectionretrydelay"></a>The wait between database connection attempts at startup. |
| `Database:MigrationTimeout` | `Database__MigrationTimeout` | duration (`[d.]hh:mm:ss`) | `00:05:00` | `00:00:01` – `00:30:00` | <a id="database-migrationtimeout"></a>How long one module may hold its migration lock, so a stuck migration fails instead of waiting forever. |

## Hosting and reverse proxies

**Trusting nothing is the default, and it matters.** Sites are resolved from the `Host`
header, so a spoofable `X-Forwarded-Host` would let a caller choose which site they are
talking to. If you put a proxy in front, name it in `Hosting:KnownProxies` or
`Hosting:KnownNetworks`.

**Sign-in security depends on this too.** Two identity rules read the client's address and
scheme, and behind a proxy they are only correct when the proxy is named:

- per-client sign-in throttling blocks an address after repeated failures, and every
  request through an unnamed proxy appears to come from the proxy, so one attacker would
  block everyone;
- the HTTPS rule refuses credentials sent over plain HTTP from other machines, and it
  cannot see that the original request was HTTPS unless it trusts `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

**Several proxies.** Name every hop you run (for example a CDN and the proxy behind it).
Forwarded values are unwound hop by hop from the nearest one, and unwinding stops at the
first address that is not named, so an unnamed hop can never choose the host.

**robots.txt under a base path.** Search engines look for `/robots.txt` at the root of a host
name only. With `Hosting:BasePath` set, forward that one address to `{BasePath}/robots.txt`
at the proxy; see [Sub-path installation](../reverse-proxy/index.md#sub-path-installation).

**Keeping the admin off client domains.** For an installation that hosts client sites, set
`Hosting:AdminHostNames` to a name only you use. If you mistype it and lose the admin, remove
the setting (or fix it) and restart: it is the only thing that confines the admin.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Hosting:BasePath` | `Hosting__BasePath` | text | *(empty)* | empty, or a path starting with `/` | <a id="hosting-basepath"></a>Serve the installation under a sub-path, e.g. `/cms`. Empty serves it at the root. |
| `Hosting:KnownProxies:<n>` | `Hosting__KnownProxies__0` | list of text | *(empty)* | IP addresses | <a id="hosting-knownproxies"></a>IP addresses of the reverse proxies whose forwarded headers are trusted. Empty trusts no forwarded header. |
| `Hosting:KnownNetworks:<n>` | `Hosting__KnownNetworks__0` | list of text | *(empty)* | CIDR ranges | <a id="hosting-knownnetworks"></a>Networks of trusted reverse proxies in CIDR form, e.g. `10.0.0.0/8`, for proxies without a fixed address. |
| `Hosting:AdminHostNames:<n>` | `Hosting__AdminHostNames__0` | list of text | *(empty)* | host names only: no scheme, port, path or wildcard, and none a site already holds | <a id="hosting-adminhostnames"></a>Host names on which the administrative surface (`/api`, `/admin`) answers, e.g. `admin.example.com`. Empty means every host name. On any other host name `/api` and `/admin` answer exactly like a missing page, so client domains never show the sign-in page; `/health` answers on every host. |
| `Hosting:PublicUrl` | `Hosting__PublicUrl` | text | *(empty)* | empty, or an absolute `http(s)` URL such as `https://cms.example.com` | <a id="hosting-publicurl"></a>The address people use to reach this installation, including any base path. Used to print complete links from `identity recovery-link` and in notification emails; the app never works out its own address from request headers. |

## Admin

The admin requires sign-in. A fresh installation is claimed through the setup wizard with a
one-time code printed in the logs, and until setup is finished whoever has that code can
become the administrator. The reference `docker-compose.yml` therefore publishes the app on
`127.0.0.1`. Finish setup first; if you then widen the binding, follow the
[security checklist](../security-checklist.md).

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Admin:PathPrefix` | `Admin__PathPrefix` | text | `/admin` | a path of one segment starting with `/` | <a id="admin-pathprefix"></a>Where the admin interface is served. Reserved ahead of every site's pages. |

## Storage

Every storage setting is checked at startup; an unusable one stops the app before it
listens, with a message that names the setting.

**S3-compatible services** include AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO and Ceph: any service that
supports conditional writes (`If-None-Match: *`). Startup checks that it does.

**Startup and readiness.** With a remote provider, startup writes, re-writes (which must be
refused), reads and deletes a small probe object under `{KeyPrefix}.quickbuilder-probe/`,
within 30 seconds. A failure stops the app before it listens and names the setting at
fault: credentials rejected, bucket or container missing, access denied, unreachable, or no
conditional writes. `/health/ready` includes a storage check (2 seconds for a remote
provider): an instance whose storage stops being writable or readable after startup reports
not ready until it recovers.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Storage:Provider` | `Storage__Provider` | text | `Local` | `Local`, `S3`, `AzureBlob` | <a id="storage-provider"></a>Where uploaded files live: `Local` (the file system), `S3` (any S3-compatible service) or `AzureBlob`, case-insensitive. Only the selected provider is loaded, and only it makes network calls. |

### Local file system

Applies when `Storage:Provider` = `Local`.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Storage:Local:Path` | `Storage__Local__Path` | text | Image: `/var/lib/quickbuilder/media`. Elsewhere: `{LocalApplicationData}/QuickBuilder/media` | an absolute path that is not, and is not inside, the application's own directory, content root or web root | <a id="storage-local-path"></a>The directory that holds uploaded files. It is created if missing and must be writable. In a container, mount persistent storage here; the reference compose file uses the `media-data` volume. |

| `Storage:S3:Region` | `Storage__S3__Region` | text | *(empty)* | — | <a id="storage-s3-region"></a>The region, e.g. `eu-west-1`. Required with S3; any value (such as `auto`) for services that ignore regions. |
| `Storage:S3:ServiceUrl` | `Storage__S3__ServiceUrl` | text | *(empty)* | empty, or an absolute `http(s)` URL | <a id="storage-s3-serviceurl"></a>The service address for anything other than AWS, e.g. `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. Empty means AWS. |
| `Storage:S3:ForcePathStyle` | `Storage__S3__ForcePathStyle` | true/false | `false` | — | <a id="storage-s3-forcepathstyle"></a>Address buckets by path rather than by host name; `true` for most self-hosted services (MinIO, Ceph). |

## Media

Every site serves its media files at `/_media/{id}.{ext}` on its own host names. The
`/_media` path is reserved on every site host: if a reverse proxy handled that path itself,
it must stop.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Media:MaxFileSizeBytes` | `Media__MaxFileSizeBytes` | whole number | `20971520` | 1024 â 1073741824 | <a id="media-maxfilesizebytes"></a>The largest file an upload may be, in bytes. The server stops receiving an upload the moment it passes this. |
| `Media:AllowedTypes` | `Media__AllowedTypes__0` | list of text | all six: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/avif`, `application/pdf` | a subset of the six default types | <a id="media-allowedtypes"></a>Which types uploads may have, decided from each file's contents. Set `Media__AllowedTypes__0`, `__1`, â¦ to narrow the list; any other type (SVG, for example) stops startup. |
| `Media:OrphanGracePeriod` | `Media__OrphanGracePeriod` | duration (`[d.]hh:mm:ss`) | `1.00:00:00` | `01:00:00` â `30.00:00:00` | <a id="media-orphangraceperiod"></a>Stored bytes with no library entry (left by a crash or a failed clean-up) are removed by an hourly sweep once they are this old. |
| `Media:MaxImagePixels` | `Media__MaxImagePixels` | whole number | `100000000` | 1000000 â 1000000000 | <a id="media-maximagepixels"></a>Images with more pixels (width Ã height) are refused at upload. Only the image header is read to decide, so an oversized image is never decoded. |

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Media:Variants:Widths` | `Media__Variants__Widths__0` | list of whole number | `320`, `640`, `960`, `1280`, `1920`, `2560` | 1 â 10 widths, ascending, each 64 â 4096 | <a id="media-variants-widths"></a>The widths published pages and the admin offer resized copies at. The smallest is the thumbnail width, made right after upload; the others are made the first time they are requested. Set `Media__Variants__Widths__0`, `__1`, â¦ to replace the list; addresses for removed widths stop working. |
| `Media:Variants:MaxConcurrent` | `Media__Variants__MaxConcurrent` | whole number | half the processor count, at least 1 | 1 â 64 | <a id="media-variants-maxconcurrent"></a>How many resized copies one instance makes at the same time. Requests beyond it wait. |
| `Media:Variants:Timeout` | `Media__Variants__Timeout` | duration (`[d.]hh:mm:ss`) | `00:00:10` | `00:00:01` â `00:01:00` | <a id="media-variants-timeout"></a>How long making one resized copy may take, waiting included. ## Site export and import

Archives kept for download in the admin are stored with the media storage provider, under
`<site>/transfers/`, and are deleted 7 days after the export finishes. A reverse proxy in
front of the app usually limits request bodies too; see
[Reverse proxy and TLS](../reverse-proxy/index.md#request-size-limits).

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SiteTransfer:MaxUploadSizeBytes` | `SiteTransfer__MaxUploadSizeBytes` | whole number | `10737418240` | 1048576 â 107374182400 | <a id="sitetransfer-maxuploadsizebytes"></a>The largest site archive the admin accepts as an upload for import, in bytes. The `sites import` command reads archives from disk and has no limit. Raise the reverse proxy's request size limit for `/api/v1/transfers/uploads` to match. |

## Trash

Files in the trash keep using storage until they are purged. To free space sooner, an
Administrator can delete them permanently or empty the trash.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Trash:RetentionDays` | `Trash__RetentionDays` | whole number | `30` | `1` – `3650` | <a id="trash-retentiondays"></a>Days deleted pages, shared components, collection items and media files stay in their site's trash before an hourly job deletes them permanently. A change applies at once to everything already in the trash. |

## Preview links

Preview links last 7 days unless the member who creates one chooses otherwise, and 30 days
at most. An hourly job deletes links that ended more than 30 days ago.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Preview:LinksValidFrom` | `Preview__LinksValidFrom` | date and time (ISO 8601, UTC) | *(empty)* | a UTC time at most one day ahead | <a id="preview-linksvalidfrom"></a>Preview links created before this time stop working, as if revoked. Set it to the current time and restart to end every existing link at once; links created afterwards work. |

## Menus

Menus have no settings. Menu limits (50 menus per site, 300 entries, three levels) are part
of the menu contract.

## Editing sessions

Editing sessions have no settings. A lock lapses 2 minutes after its editor stops answering
and becomes stale after 30 minutes without a change. Locks are kept in PostgreSQL, so they
work across instances without a shared cache.

## Email

Outgoing email sends form notifications and the test email. Every email setting is
optional: leave `Email:Smtp:Host` empty and the installation sends no email at all.

Startup stops, naming the setting, when `Email:Smtp:Host` is set without a valid
`Email:Smtp:From`, or when a value is out of range. It also stops when `Email:Smtp:Security`
is `None` and a user name is set for a mail server on another machine: the password would
cross the network unencrypted. On the same machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) that is
allowed.

Links in notifications point at the submission in the admin and are built from
`Hosting:PublicUrl` and `Admin:PathPrefix`, never from a request. With email on and
`Hosting:PublicUrl` empty, emails say "Open Submissions in the admin" without a link, and
startup logs a warning.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Email:Smtp:Host` | `Email__Smtp__Host` | text | *(empty)* | — | <a id="email-smtp-host"></a>The mail server's host name or address. Empty turns email off: no connection is made and editors see that notifications are off. |
| `Email:Smtp:Port` | `Email__Smtp__Port` | whole number | `587` | 1 – 65535 | <a id="email-smtp-port"></a>The mail server's port. Usually 587 with `StartTls`, 465 with `SslOnConnect`. |
| `Email:Smtp:Security` | `Email__Smtp__Security` | one of the listed values | `StartTls` | `None`, `StartTls`, `SslOnConnect` | <a id="email-smtp-security"></a>How the connection is encrypted. `StartTls` encrypts before anything is sent and the server must offer it; `SslOnConnect` uses TLS from the first byte. The server's certificate must be trusted by the container. `None` with a user name is allowed only for a mail server on the same machine. |
| `Email:Smtp:UserName` | `Email__Smtp__UserName` | text | *(empty)* | — | <a id="email-smtp-username"></a>The sign-in name. Empty means no sign-in. |
| `Email:Smtp:Password` | `Email__Smtp__Password` | text | *(empty)* | — | <a id="email-smtp-password"></a>The sign-in password. It is never stored in the database or shown in the admin. **Secret.** Provide it through an environment variable or a secret store, never in a file committed to version control. |
| `Email:Smtp:From` | `Email__Smtp__From` | text | *(empty)* | an email address | <a id="email-smtp-from"></a>The sender address, such as `website@example.com`. Required when `Email:Smtp:Host` is set. |
| `Email:Smtp:FromName` | `Email__Smtp__FromName` | text | `QuickBuilder` | at most 100 characters | <a id="email-smtp-fromname"></a>The sender name shown to recipients. |
| `Email:Smtp:Timeout` | `Email__Smtp__Timeout` | duration (`[d.]hh:mm:ss`) | `00:00:30` | `00:00:05` – `00:05:00` | <a id="email-smtp-timeout"></a>How long one sending attempt may take. |

## Forms

Every request to `/_forms` counts, valid or not. Over a limit, the visitor sees the form
again with their values and a message to wait; the response says how long. Counts are kept
in the database, so every instance shares them, and are deleted after an hour. IPv6
addresses are grouped by their /64 network, as sign-in throttling groups them.

**Behind a reverse proxy, name it in `Hosting:KnownProxies` or `Hosting:KnownNetworks`.**
Otherwise every visitor arrives from the proxy's address and they all share one limit: a
busy site would refuse genuine enquiries after the first few in a minute.

### Rate limits

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Forms:RateLimit:PerMinute` | `Forms__RateLimit__PerMinute` | whole number | `5` | 1 â 1000 | <a id="forms-ratelimit-perminute"></a>Form submissions one visitor address may send to one site in a minute. Every request counts, valid or not. |
| `Forms:RateLimit:PerHour` | `Forms__RateLimit__PerHour` | whole number | `30` | 1 â 10000, and at least `Forms:RateLimit:PerMinute` | <a id="forms-ratelimit-perhour"></a>Form submissions one visitor address may send to one site in an hour. |

## Cache

The cache never decides what visitors see: each page's cache key includes version numbers
read from the database on every request, so a publish is visible on every instance at its
next request without any shared cache.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Cache:MemoryLimitMegabytes` | `Cache__MemoryLimitMegabytes` | whole number | `256` | `16` – `16384` | <a id="cache-memorylimitmegabytes"></a>Upper bound on each instance's in-memory cache, in megabytes. Rendered public pages take nearly all of it; when full, the least recently used pages are dropped and rendered again on their next request. |

## Telemetry

Tracing and metrics are always instrumented (that is where the trace id in the logs comes
from), but nothing is exported unless you name a collector. An offline installation behaves
identically to a connected one.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Telemetry:OtlpEndpoint` | `Telemetry__OtlpEndpoint` | text | *(empty)* | empty, or the collector's URL, e.g. `http://otel-collector:4317` | <a id="telemetry-otlpendpoint"></a>The OpenTelemetry (OTLP) collector to export traces and metrics to. Empty means no exporter is registered and nothing leaves the process. |
| `Telemetry:ServiceName` | `Telemetry__ServiceName` | text | `quickbuilder` | — | <a id="telemetry-servicename"></a>The service name on exported traces and metrics. |

## Logging

Logs are structured JSON on standard output. Every entry carries a `TraceId`, the same value
returned in the `traceId` of an error response, so "it failed, here is the id" is enough to
find the entry. Logs never contain credentials, secrets, personal data or content bodies.

### Log levels

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Serilog:MinimumLevel:Default` | `Serilog__MinimumLevel__Default` | text | `Information` | `Verbose`, `Debug`, `Information`, `Warning`, `Error`, `Fatal` | <a id="serilog-minimumlevel-default"></a>The lowest level written to the log for every component without an override. |
| `Serilog:MinimumLevel:Override:<Namespace>` | `Serilog__MinimumLevel__Override__<Namespace>` | map of text | `Microsoft`: `Warning`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore`: `Warning`, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`: `Warning`, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command`: `Warning`, `QuickBuilder`: `Information` | `Verbose`, `Debug`, `Information`, `Warning`, `Error`, `Fatal` | <a id="serilog-minimumlevel-override"></a>The lowest level for one component and everything under it, by namespace, e.g. `Serilog__MinimumLevel__Override__QuickBuilder=Debug`. |
